clauses.label: S ection  1.
clauses.text:
S ection  1. Any suggestion, invention, or scientific achievement by 
a member of the armed forces that contributes to the efficiency, econ­
omy, or other improvement of operations of the Government of the 
United States through its adoption or use by an executive department 
or agency other than the executive department having jurisdiction 
over the armed force of the member concerned may be the basis for 
honorary recognition or a cash award by the Secretary of Transporta­
tion in the case of a member of the Coast Guard when it is not operat­
ing as a service in the Navy or by the Secretary of Defense in the case 
of any other member of the .armed forces.
S ec . | |  An executive department or agency that adopts or uses the 
suggestion, invention, or scientific achievement o f a member of the 
armed forces who is not under its jurisdiction may recommend to the 
Department of Defense or to the Department of Transportation, as 
appropriate, a cash award or honorary recognition o f the member 
and shall justify its recommendation with appropriate documentation 
and explanation o f how the suggestion, invention, or scientific achieve­
ment contributes to the efficiency, economy, or other improvement of 
the operations of the Government of the United States. Awards shall 
be made under regulations to be prescribed by the Secretary of Defense 
or the Secretary of Transportation, as appropriate. The regulations 
of the Department o f Defense and Department o f Transportation 
may include designations of officials to whom authority for receiving, 
evaluating, and making awards may .  be assigned.
Sec. -3 .. No cash awards hereunder for a single suggestion, invention, 
or scientific achievement may exceed $25,000 regardless of the number 
o f agencies or departments which may adopt or use the suggestion, 
invention, or scientific achievement.

clauses.label: S ec. 4.
clauses.text:
S ec. 4. Funds to cover the costs o f cash awards to members of the 
armed forces shall be transferred from the account o f any executive 
department or agency which recommends the award to the appropriate 
account o f the Department o f Transportation or the Department of 
Defense, as the case may be. When several executive departments or 
agencies benefit from the adoption or use o f the suggestion, invention, 
or scientific achievement, the amount transferred from each such 
benefiting department or agency to the Department of Transportation 
or the Department of Defense to cover the proportionate share o f the 
cost of the cash award shall be determined under procedures prescribed 
by the Civil Service Commission in accordance with the same guide­
lines and standards applying to awards to civilian employees.

versions.research_rationale: basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search (EO 13306 precedent). EO 11438 (signed 1968-12-03; 33 FR 18085; held official FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11438.txt, read in full) prescribes procedures for interdepartmental honorary recognition and cash awards to armed forces members (sec. 1 authorization, sec. 2 recommendation process, sec. 3 $25,000 cap, sec. 4 transfer of funds). The dossier's one 'whole' clause also spans the authority recital; I split it into four section clauses with inventory_overrides because the two amendments hit different sections. EO 13306 pattern conditions tested for this order: (1) ACT records and dossier missing lines: one ACT record (ACT:EO:11438>EO:13286, sec. 63) and one actor text (ACTOR_TEXT:EO:12107, listed under the missing line 'target provision not located: EO:12107'); I read both: EO 12107 sec. 2-101 is a bulk substitution of 'Office of Personnel Management' for 'Civil Service Commission' (EO 11438 is on its list; effective 1979-01-01 under sec. 2-404) and EO 13286 sec. 63 swaps Transportation for Homeland Security in secs. 1, 2 and 4 (effective 2003-03-01 under sec. 92); both are partial amendments and both are attached as later_events on the clauses they touch, so no ACT record or missing line is left unresolved; the three standing missing lines (judgment needed for the current predicate; current-law lead lacks an original-source sha256; no attributed legal-text slice for the current-law pointer) are read and ruled out as bases: the basis of this claim is the held original text, not the lead, and the lead is used only as corroboration. (2) Own-term end: none (own_terms is empty). (3) The dossier has no conflicts. (4) The selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) carry no coverage warning; they cover the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition through 2026-10-09; laws of 2026-10-10..14 are not reflected, a stated limit), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 and the OFR catalog with 17,521 saved order texts (checked 2026-10-19). Corroboration read: the 10 U.S.C. 1124 note in release point 119-121 prints sections 1 to 4 in the amended form, naming the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Office of Personnel Management, with the status line 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 12107 ... Ex. Ord. No. 13286, section 63' and no ending statement (jobs/current-law/output/USC_EO_NOTES.jsonl, note id ida89b0b8b-3a6f-11f1-a58a-d8db54b14ab5); 5 CFR part 451 cites EO 11438 as authority and 5 CFR 451.101 and 451.104 refer to its sec. 4 (citation leads only). D6 / later events searched: EDGES.csv edges naming EO 11438 as target are EO 12107 (1978-12-28, 2 rows) and EO 13286 (2003-02-28, 5 rows) only; a grep of the 6,652 held fr-originals texts (through EO 14435) finds only EO 13286 besides the order (EO 12107 lists it by number); no later order amends, revokes or supersedes it. EO 13286 sec. 63's own savings wording is in sec. 63 of a different order and does not touch EO 11438; EO 13286 sec. 92 gives 2003-03-01 as its effective date. Limit stated plainly: continuation is inferred from the original, the two attached amendments, the absence of any ending in the bounded searches and the current Code note; the text of 5 CFR part 451 is not held as an attributed slice and is not asserted.

Executive Order 11438 of December 3, 1968 ( ‘‘Prescribing Procedures 
Governing Interdepartmental Cash Awards to the Members of the Armed 
Forces’’), as amended, is further amended by: 
(a) striking ‘‘the Secretary of Transportation ’’ in sections 1 and 2 and 
inserting ‘‘the Secretary of Homeland Security’’ in lieu thereof; and

sections 2 and 4 and inserting ‘‘the Department of Homeland Security ’’ 
in lieu thereof.
